recommended_subsections: Overview and how to use this section
Standards and framework alignment (basis of selection and mapping)
Targets register (targets, baselines, progress, and status)
Scope, boundary, and coverage (inclusions, exclusions, and reconciliation)
Methodology and calculation approach (high-level steps and key assumptions)
Data quality, controls, and change management (restatements and comparability)
Assurance (what is assured, level, scope, and where to find the opinion)
recommended_order: Navigational overview (subsections list) and purpose statement
Standards anchor and selection approach (materiality/relevance lens; linkage to strategy/risk/governance pillars)
Explain table conventions (units, symbols, placeholders, mapping fields, assurance markers)
Targets register table (linked to metrics; progress tracking)
Disaggregation tables (only for complex metrics where segmentation is decision-useful)
Coverage and reconciliation block (eligible population to reported subset; exclusions listed)
Methodology summary (steps, assumptions, boundary approach; pointer to full methodology)
Data quality and limitations (uncertainty drivers; comparability; recalculation triggers)
Assurance note (scope and limitations; distinction between assured and non-assured content)

recommended_tables.purpose: Single source of truth for all disclosed metrics with definitions, values/status, provenance, and mapping.
suggested_columns: Internal source (system/reporting owner or repository reference)
formatting_rules: Repeat header on each page if paginated
Right-align numeric columns; keep text columns left-aligned
Allow multi-line cells for definitions and qualitative values
Use consistent placeholder terms for missing/not applicable items

recommended_tables.purpose: Document targets linked to metrics, including baseline, scope, progress tracking, and status.
suggested_columns: Target timeframe (described without numeric commitments in template form)
Current status (on track / in progress / planned / not reported)
External reference (if aligned to a standard/initiative)
formatting_rules: Use neutral status language; avoid performance claims
Ensure each target has an explicit measurement method and boundary statement

recommended_tables.purpose: Provide decision-useful breakdowns for complex metrics by category (e.g., business line, geography, sector, asset class, product type).
formatting_rules: Include a total row where meaningful
Define the classification/taxonomy used in a footnote or notes column

recommended_tables.table_name: Coverage and Reconciliation (Optional but recommended for scoped metrics)
recommended_tables.purpose: Bridge from eligible population to reported subset to make boundary decisions transparent.
suggested_columns: Reconciliation line item (start value, exclusions, adjustments, final reported perimeter)
formatting_rules: Present as a clear step-down structure (start → exclusions/adjustments → final)
Tie each line item to a footnote where conventions are non-obvious

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Visualize composition of a key metric across a chosen segmentation dimension.
design_rules: Keep labels consistent with disaggregation table categories
Reference the figure with a single directional sentence in the narrative
Do not introduce new definitions in the figure; definitions live in tables

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Illustrate how the reporting perimeter is derived from the eligible population.
design_rules: Mirror the reconciliation table line items
Use a consistent assurance marker approach if applicable

recommended_figures_or_diagrams.purpose: Highlight the most decision-relevant headline outputs while keeping the table as the authoritative source.
design_rules: Include only metrics already present in the register
Include boundary/coverage qualifier in small text

required_narrative_blocks: Purpose and standards anchor: why metrics and targets are disclosed and how this section supports decision-usefulness.
Metric selection and linkage: how metrics were selected (relevance/materiality lens) and how targets relate to metrics for progress tracking.
How to read the register: explanation of columns, mapping to report pillars, units, placeholders for missing data, and assurance markers.
Boundary and period statement: clear statement of reporting period, organisational boundary approach, and general coverage principles.
Limitations and comparability: key uncertainty drivers, data maturity, and conditions under which recalculations/restatements may occur.
optional_narrative_blocks: Framework continuity note: how metrics align with other commonly used frameworks to support comparability across reporting cycles.
Governance and controls summary: ownership, review/validation steps, and system enhancements relevant to metric reliability.
Methodology pointer: where detailed methodologies, formulas, and basis of preparation are published.
Assurance summary note: what assurance covers, level of assurance, and where the assurance report/opinion can be accessed.
output_structure_rules: Begin with a short subsection list (navigation) before substantive content.
Keep narrative paragraphs short and table-referential; tables are the primary evidence base.
Use a consistent two-level heading hierarchy (section title + numbered subsections).
Ensure every metric and target includes: definition, scope/boundary, reporting-period value/status, provenance, and mapping to report pillar/section.
Use consistent terminology for scope, boundary, coverage, and exclusions across all tables and notes.
Separate assured vs non-assured information using a generic indicator and a single consolidated explanatory note.
When including methodology, present: (a) stepwise bullet logic, then (b) a concise formula representation (generic, not copied).
Use footnotes for technical conventions and classification references; avoid embedding long technical digressions in the main narrative.
